rubrics.criterion: In spectrwm.c, the mapping refresh (update_region_mapping and its update_mapping caller path) no longer performs a window's map or unmap transition itself: the per-window X transition -- map/unmap of the frame, the client window and the debug window, the mapping/unmapping counters, the mapped flag and the paired WM_STATE restamp with the a_state property change -- is now carried out by code hosted on the window record (a function whose owner parameter is the ws_win being transitioned), whatever that function is named in the repair.
rubrics.rationale: This is the heart of the envy relation at the walk site: the region walker legitimately decides which windows are visible, but the transition itself belongs to the window. The rubric is instance-specific because the exact fields (frame, id, debug, mapping, unmapping, mapped, state) and the a_state pairing only occur in this duplicated transition code.

rubrics.criterion: After the repair, update_region_mapping still performs its coordinator job for exactly its own region: it derives the region's workspace and visibility filter (the mof/main-identity and WINDOCK gating), walks only that region's window list, and triggers each window's transition in the same visit order -- the repair re-homes the transition, not the visibility decision.
rubrics.rationale: Move-method repairs at this site can easily overreach by pushing screen- or region-level bookkeeping into the window. This item pins the split that makes the repair correct rather than merely smaller: decisions about which windows belong to the region stay where the per-region state lives.

rubrics.criterion: In the focus keybinding dispatch (focus in spectrwm.c), resolving a focus candidate no longer re-implements the window-side resolution steps field-by-field inside the dispatcher: following a candidate's main/focus_redirect chain (bounded in the same way and stopping on NULL, hidden or invalid targets) and probing a candidate's urgency (the SWM_Q_IGNOREURGENT quirks gate before the WM_HINTS urgency and demands-attention test) are performed by window-owned code paths, so the dispatcher seeds candidates per binding path and hands the resolved window over to focus setting.
rubrics.rationale: The dispatch function is the largest envy site; its foreign accesses concentrate exactly in the redirect chase and urgency probes that appear three-plus times across its binding paths. The rubric names the responsibilities rather than any helper signature, so delegating to pre-existing functions or new owner functions both satisfy it.

rubrics.criterion: The stacking-layer recomputation for the focus family after a focus change -- deciding each family window's layer from raised/desktop/below/fullscreen/maximized/dock/floating/tiled in that precedence, applying the rule that a related window stays at or above its main's layer, and stamping the resulting layer -- is window-owned code after the repair; the dispatcher only identifies the family (the main window and its related windows) rather than computing and writing layer values itself.
rubrics.rationale: Layer decisions read and write window state through about a dozen distinct fields; this is the portion of the dispatcher that duplicates the window's own layer logic. Keeping the family discovery in the driver while moving the per-window computation is the semantically meaningful repair.

rubrics.criterion: In the iconify/hide path, dropping focus from the targeted window -- the invalid window/workspace validation with dangling-reference cleanup, clearing the screen's focus mirror and the workspace's focus/focus_raise mirrors under the same conditions, re-deriving stacking and priority only when always_raise or focus_raise demands it, and the minimal-border floating check with its border/gravity adjustment -- is performed by window-owned code rather than re-implemented inside the keybinding handler.
rubrics.rationale: The focus-drop logic is the window's own transition; the handler's job is deciding which window hides and which focus replaces it. The concrete guard chains (invalid ws/win, focus_raise clearance, minimal-border geometry move) are instance-specific and gradeable from the patch without prescribing helper names.

rubrics.criterion: Applying the hide/hide-state flag flip to a window still keeps the whole EWMH state machine on one code path owned by the window side: flipping EWMH_F_HIDDEN, keeping iconified-list membership in sync with it, reloading or storing floating geometry on the transitions (unhide reload for floating windows, above/below and maximized/fullscreen geometry bookkeeping), clearing EWMH_F_MAXIMIZED under the same condition, and rebuilding the _NET_WM_STATE atom set from the window's full flag word before publishing to the window's X window.
rubrics.rationale: This transition was re-implemented inside the handler flag-by-flag; splitting any part of it out of the driver but not the rest would leave a majority-envied handler while still letting a mechanical extraction pass. The criterion is answerable by inspecting which functions now own the flag word writes and the atom rebuild.

rubrics.criterion: The re-implemented transition code inside the three driver functions is genuinely removed rather than bypassed: after the repair no duplicated copy of the map/unmap+WM_STATE statements, the redirect chase, the urgency test, the layer precedence chain, the focus-drop guard chain, or the flag-flip/atom-rebuild statements remains inside focus, update_region_mapping or iconify -- each exists exactly once, in its owner-side home.
rubrics.rationale: A plausible partial repair delegates the new calls but leaves the old inlined statements in place under a false branch or as dead code. This coupled fact cannot be split from the core resolution without destroying its meaning: the relation is resolved by relocation in single copy.

rubrics.criterion: The window-transition code paths that other flows use remain coherent after the repair: window transfer/move (transfer_win/send_to_rg paths), workspace switching and stacking (switch_workspace, stack and raise-path callers such as raise_focus and the maximize-related toggles) still reach the same owner-side transition implementations the drivers now delegate to, and perform their own sequencing (focus seeding, apply_unfocus, stacking refresh, mapping update) exactly as before.
rubrics.rationale: The clean tree already routes several flows through the transition helpers the drivers duplicated; a repair that special-cases only the three envy sites and leaves collaborators on divergent copies would strand the duplication elsewhere in the file. This is specific to this instance's collaboration graph.

rubrics.criterion: After hiding a window, the replacement focus resolution keeps the two modes intact: when pointer follow applies, the replacement candidate resolved from the current region is chased through its own redirect chain before focus is set; when pointer follow does not apply, no replacement is forced on the user and the direct focus handoff happens exactly once per activation.
rubrics.rationale: The hide transition ends in a mode split that the duplicated chase code sits inside; a repair that unifies the code paths can silently move the chase to the non-follow branch or run it twice. The observable contract here is specific: exactly one set_focus per activation with the same candidate in each mode.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not leave behind scaffolding that existed only to support the displaced copies inside the drivers: hoisted pointer temporaries that merely cache member accesses (for example the screen/region-owned addressability hoists over the iconified list and region workspace or bar pointers), loop/counter temporaries used by nothing else, or write-only bookkeeping locals -- no unused or dead local survives and the tree still compiles without new warnings under -Wall -Wextra -Wshadow.
rubrics.rationale: This injection added genuinely used bookkeeping locals on every host to keep counts; when the copies move out, those locals become dead weight. Warning-free compilation is owned by nobody else here: the build gate only checks exit status, so this rubric owns warning hygiene for this instance.

rubrics.criterion: Diagnostic output lines that the displaced copies carried (the repeated mapping/state labels, focus/redirect debug lines and flag-change lines that already exist inside the owner-side implementations) are not kept duplicated in both the coordinator and the owner-side code after the repair.
rubrics.rationale: The copies reproduce the owner functions' debug strings verbatim, so after a correct relocation the driver must not anymore print the same state transitions twice per event. This is a concrete, mechanically checkable duplication left by exactly this instance's inlining.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not decouple ICCCM WM_STATE from the X transition: no code path maps or unmaps a window without restamping its WM_STATE as NORMAL or ICONIC in the same operation, and no path restamps state without performing the corresponding map/unmap -- in particular reparented windows (frame != XCB_WINDOW_NONE) keep the skip behavior exactly as before.
rubrics.rationale: WM_STATE staleness is this repository's own historical bug class (the pinned tree's most recent fixes address stale WM_STATE on startup), and the duplicated transition code is precisely where the pairing could get split during extraction. The paired-write invariant is gradeable from the patch hunk by hunk.

rubrics.criterion: Iconified-list membership keeps mirroring the window's hidden flag exactly: a window is inserted on hide (and unmapped together with its frame/debug windows) and removed on unhide (with floating geometry reloaded for windows that float), with no path that flips the flag without updating the list or vice versa, and both changes remain part of one hide/unhide operation.
rubrics.rationale: The flag flip and list bookkeeping were duplicated into the hide handler; a repair that moves only the property write while leaving list manipulation in the dispatcher can hit windows one flip out of sync. The double-entry requirement is specific to this instance's state machine.

rubrics.criterion: The re-homed code does not reorder or weaken the evaluation order of the guard chains: validation of the targeted window and its workspace (and the dangling-reference cleanup it triggers) still precedes any focus-mirror clearing; urgency is still evaluated only for windows whose quirks do not ignore it; the redirect chase still stops at the first NULL, hidden or invalid target and remains bounded by the workspace's normal-window count; the minimal-border geometry adjustment still tests the same five floating conditions with short-circuiting.
rubrics.rationale: These chains were flattened and duplicated across three drivers; short-circuit reordering is the most plausible way a relocation changes behavior without changing any single statement. Each condition named here is observable directly in the solver's patch text.

rubrics.criterion: After delegation, layer computation produces the same values as before for every window of the focus family: the precedence order raised, desktop, below, fullscreen, maximized, dock, floating, tiled is unchanged, a non-main window never ends below its main's already-stamped layer, the family walk covers the main window exactly once and then every related window of the same main exactly once per focus change, and no layer is stamped twice for the same window in one refresh.
rubrics.rationale: The family layer walk visits two overlapping sets (the main window and its related windows); a repair that delegates per-window layering but restructures the walk can easily double-stamp or skip the main. The overlap condition is unique to this instance's stacking code.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not recreate the same foreign-owner coupling elsewhere: code moved out of the three drivers ends up hosted by the data it operates on (window-side state as window-owned parameters), rather than being parked on a new global-style home or on the screen/region side wholesale -- in particular no new function keeps doing a window's transitions while carrying the screen or region as its owner parameter.
rubrics.rationale: Mechanical extraction that threads only the original host parameter through a new helper reproduces the same relation one level down. Graders can check the owner parameter of each new function in the solver patch against the fields its body dominates; this is the failure mode most likely for this instance's solver.
